name: Town Centre (Mole and Jetty)
description: The compact colonial core wrapped around the Mole and the famous jetty, lined with German-era landmarks, bakeries, cafes and shops. Everything is walkable, the seafront is on your doorstep, and most guesthouses and restaurants cluster here for easy nomad living.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable cafes, seafront strolls and central convenience
pros: Walkable to cafes, shops and the sea
Best choice of guesthouses and restaurants
cons: Busier in the December-to-March holiday season

name: Vineta
tagline: Leafy coastal residential area north of centre
description: A settled, well-kept residential district hugging the coast just north of the Centre, popular with families and longer-stay visitors. Quiet streets, easy beach access and a short walk or drive into town make it a comfortable, calm base away from the tourist bustle.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting calm, beach access and a homely base
pros: Close to the coast and beaches

name: Kramersdorf
tagline: Established inland suburb of quiet homes
description: A tidy, established residential suburb set back from the seafront, made up of family homes on orderly grid streets. It offers better-value accommodation than the coast, a settled local feel and a straightforward drive or cycle into the Centre for work and errands.
bestFor: Budget-conscious nomads wanting quiet, spacious and better-value housing
cons: Set back from the beach and cafes
Car or bike needed for town trips

name: Mondesa and Tamariskia
description: The historically local townships east of the Centre, home to much of Swakopmund's Namibian community and its most authentic everyday culture. Township tours, local eateries and lively markets reveal a very different, warmer side of town beyond the colonial postcard core.
bestFor: Culturally curious travellers seeking genuine local life and community
